items.markdown:
A Thailand retirement visa costs around `1,900 THB to 5,000 THB` for the official visa or extension, but requires holding at least 800,000 THB in a bank account or showing a monthly income of 65,000 THB. You can apply through the official [Thai E-Visa Website](https://www.thaievisa.go.th/) or an immigration office.[](https://thailandelitevisa.com/thailand-retirement-visa-complete-guide/) [[1]](https://thailandelitevisa.com/thailand-retirement-visa-complete-guide/)[[2]](https://wise.com/gb/blog/thai-retirement-visa)

Visa and Government Fees

- **Single-Entry Non-O-A Visa:** ~2,000 THB (applied from abroad)
- **Annual Visa Extension:** 1,900 THB (renewed inside Thailand)
- **Single Re-Entry Permit:** 1,000 THB (or 3,800 THB for multiple entries)[](https://thailandelitevisa.com/thailand-retirement-visa-complete-guide/) 

Financial Proof Requirements

- **Bank Deposit Option:** Keep 800,000 THB in a Thai bank account.
- **Monthly Income Option:** Prove a monthly income or pension of at least 65,000 THB.
- **Combination Option:** Mix annual income and bank savings to total 800,000 THB per year.[](https://www.thaiembassy.com/thailand-visa/retirement-visa) [[1]](https://www.thaiembassy.com/thailand-visa/retirement-visa)

Additional Costs

- **Health Insurance:** Mandatory coverage for certain visa types (like Non-OA), often costing 10,000 to 40,000+ THB per year depending on your age.
- **Document Fees:** Police clearance certificates, medical checks, and translations usually add 2,000 to 5,000 THB.[](https://thailandelitevisa.com/thailand-retirement-visa-complete-guide/)
